Pentagon probe found that the Feb. 28 US missile strike on an Iranian elementary school in Minab — killing 123 children — resulted from a cascade of failures.
Outdated intelligence that still classified the school as an IRGC facility, compressed timelines as the administration demanded 1,000+ strikes in 24 hours, overreliance on Palantir's Maven AI system (which personnel wrongly expected to flag stale data), and Hegseth's 90% cuts to civilian-harm-mitigation teams. 
The site had visibly operated as a school for nearly a decade, was on Google Maps, and had its own website. 
UN report this week said the failures "went beyond negligence" and may constitute war crimes. 
The Pentagon investigation has been effectively complete for months but remains unreleased. 
The administration still hasn't publicly accepted responsibility.
Source: Bloomberg

Delayed Taiwan weapons sales are damaging Anduril, CEO Luckey says
Trump’s delay in approving a $14 billion arms package for Taiwan is affecting Anduril’s business, Palmer Luckey, founder of US defense tech firm Anduril, said on Saturday, as quoted by Reuters.
The package has been held up for months. After meeting China’s Xi Jinping in May, Trump described it as a “very good negotiating chip.” 
Luckey, who has reportedly spoken with Trump, JD Vance and Marco Rubio about the issue, said the administration is weighing the potential fallout — including China’s leverage over rare earths. 
He called Trump’s position “a really difficult situation.”
Anduril’s Altius drones are already in use by Taiwan, and the two sides are jointly producing the Barracuda-500 cruise missile. 
China has sanctioned Luckey for selling weapons to the island it considers an inseparable part of its territory.
